_meta.source: MOE fees and financial assistance pages, ITE and polytechnic fee schedules, autonomous university subsidised fee tables, CPF Education Scheme, SkillsFuture Credit, and the four self help groups
_meta.units: Singapore dollars, for a Singapore Citizen, before assistance
_meta.notes: EVERY FIGURE HERE IS PROVISIONAL AND NEEDS A HUMAN AGAINST THE NAMED PAGE. Fee schedules change annually and vary by course and by school, so bands are used rather than point figures wherever the real number varies: a precise wrong number is worse than an honest range. Costs are listed before help on purpose, because a page that opened with reassurance would read as a sales pitch. The four truths at the end are the actual guidance; the tables are the evidence for them.

costs.label: Secondary school, government or government aided
costs.misc: Standard miscellaneous fees on top, usually under 25 a month
costs.note: For a Singapore Citizen. Permanent Residents and international students pay published higher rates.

costs.label: Independent school
costs.misc: Varies by school, and published by each
costs.note: The Independent School Bursary exists precisely because this figure is large, and it reaches well into middle incomes.

costs.label: Junior college or Millennia Institute
costs.misc: Miscellaneous fees usually under 30 a month
costs.note: Three years at Millennia Institute rather than two, so the total is one more year of the same small number.

costs.label: ITE, Nitec or Higher Nitec
costs.misc: Plus a one time registration fee and course materials
costs.note: The lowest fee of any post secondary route, and the ITE bursaries reduce it further.

costs.label: Polytechnic diploma
costs.misc: Three years for most diplomas, so budget for three
costs.note: Before any bursary. A family on the lower income tiers can end up paying a small fraction of this.

costs.label: Arts institution diploma or degree
costs.misc: Materials and studio costs are real and are not in the fee
costs.note: Published per course. There are bursaries specific to the arts institutions, and the materials cost is the one families forget.

costs.label: Degree at a local autonomous university
costs.misc: More for medicine, dentistry and law, and four years for most degrees
costs.note: Subsidised rate for a Singapore Citizen. The Tuition Fee Loan covers most of it and charges no interest while studying.

help.label: MOE Financial Assistance Scheme
help.what: School fees, standard miscellaneous fees, textbooks, uniforms, and subsidies for transport and meals.
help.who: Singapore Citizens in government and government aided schools, on household income criteria.
help.howMuch: In practice this takes the cost of secondary school close to nothing.
help.howToGet: One form from the school's general office, once a year. The form teacher can start it.

help.label: Edusave
help.what: An account in the student's own name, topped up every year, for enrichment and approved programmes.
help.who: Every Singapore Citizen in school. Nothing to apply for.
help.howMuch: An annual contribution, plus awards and bursaries paid into the same account.
help.howToGet: It is already there. The school can say what the balance is and what it can be spent on.

help.label: Post Secondary Education Account
help.what: Where the Edusave balance goes at the end of secondary school, to be spent on approved post secondary fees.
help.who: Singapore Citizens. It can be used for a sibling's fees as well as your own.
help.howMuch: Whatever was left over, plus government top ups.
help.howToGet: Automatic. Fee payment through the institution can draw on it directly.

help.label: Bursaries at ITE, polytechnic and university
help.what: Money that reduces the fee and does not have to be paid back.
help.who: Income tiered, and the tiers reach further up than most families assume.
help.howMuch: At the lower tiers a large part of the fee, and at middle incomes still a real amount.
help.howToGet: Applied for through the institution, usually in the first weeks. Deadlines are early and easy to miss.

help.label: Tuition Fee Loan
help.what: A loan for most of the subsidised fee at a polytechnic or a university.
help.who: Available broadly, not only on low income.
help.howMuch: Up to most of the fee, with no interest charged while still studying.
help.howToGet: Through the institution at enrolment. A guarantor is needed.

help.label: CPF Education Scheme
help.what: Paying fees from a parent's or a sibling's CPF Ordinary Account, repaid with interest after graduating.
help.who: Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents at approved institutions.
help.howMuch: Up to a share of the account balance, per the scheme's limits.
help.howToGet: An application through CPF, with the student agreeing to repay.

help.label: The self help groups and community funds
help.what: Bursaries and tuition support from CDAC, MENDAKI, SINDA and the Eurasian Association.
help.who: By community, and each publishes its own criteria.
help.howMuch: Varies, and can be held at the same time as a school or institution bursary.
help.howToGet: Directly, and separately from the school. Ask, because nobody will offer.

help.label: The school's own welfare fund
help.what: The quiet money for a camp fee, a trip, a pair of shoes, a laptop.
help.who: Anybody in the school with a need, decided in the school.
help.howMuch: Small amounts, quickly, and often without a form.
help.howToGet: Ask the form teacher or the year head. This is the fastest help in the system.

help.label: SkillsFuture Credit, later
help.what: Credit for courses across a working life, with a larger top up in mid career.
help.who: Singapore Citizens, from twenty five, with the mid career top up from forty.
help.howMuch: An opening amount, periodic top ups, and a substantial mid career addition.
help.howToGet: Nothing to apply for. It sits in an account until it is used.

truths.head: The fee is not the barrier it looks like
truths.body: Every route after secondary school has a bursary attached to it, and the income tiers reach further up than families expect. The most expensive route also has the largest loan behind it, interest free while studying.

truths.head: Nobody offers. Everybody has to ask
truths.body: Almost all of this is applied for, once, on a form, in the first weeks of a school year. A family that does not know a scheme exists is not offered it, which is why knowing the names on this page is worth money.

truths.head: The cheapest route is not the least ambitious one
truths.body: ITE costs the least and its graduates start earning earliest. Four years of pay while another route is still paying fees is a real advantage, and it is not an argument against the other routes.

truths.head: Money is a reason to ask, not to stop
truths.body: A family that decides a route is unaffordable without asking has closed a door the system left open. The ECG counsellor and the school's general office both know exactly which forms apply.
